title: Mess store inventory in C++

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own project brief, code, tests and rubric for mess store inventory in c++, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

brief: The mess store keeps rice, dal, oil and milk packets. Build its inventory class in C++: stock goes up when supplies arrive, down when the kitchen takes them, and a LOW report lists what must be reordered. You implement the class declared in the header; the driver handles input.
requirements: RECEIVE adds stock and creates new items; ISSUE takes stock only if enough is there, otherwise nothing changes.
REORDER sets the level below which an item counts as low.
LOW lists items below their level as stock/level, sorted by name, including items with no stock at all.
Quantities are whole numbers from 1 to 999999.
io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `RECEIVE <item> <qty>` | `<item> stock <n>` |
| `ISSUE <item> <qty>` | `<item> stock <n>` or `error: only <n> <item> in stock` |
| `REORDER <item> <level>` | `<item> reorder at <level>` |
| `LOW` | `<item> <stock>/<level>` lines, or `nothing to reorder` |

Anything else: `error: bad command <line>`.

milestones.title: Stock in and out
milestones.instructions: Implement `receive`, `issue` and `stock`. A failed issue must not change anything.
hints: stock_[item] += qty creates the item with 0 first if it is new.
Use find in const functions: operator[] would insert a missing key.

milestones.title: Reorder report
milestones.instructions: Implement `setReorder` and `low`. Items with a level but no stock are low too.
hints: Loop over reorder_, not stock_, so items never received still appear.
std::map already iterates in sorted key order.

rubric.criterion: Hidden tests pass: every command prints exactly the expected output.
Inventory's maps are private; const member functions never insert keys; a failed ISSUE changes nothing.
Readable names, small functions and clear error handling (AI feedback, advice only).

extensions: Track the date of each receipt and issue first-in, first-out.
Print the total value of stock given prices per unit.
